title: [review] project-LICHEN-6mij: coap_oscore_authorize_mutating returns coap_oscore_send_unauthorized which already sends response; OK for single-error-path calls but register error case for 4.29 sends unprotected response even for OSCORE requests in deaddrop_post rate-limit path
description:
In coap_dtn.c:137-138, when a rate-limited deaddrop_post fails for an OSCORE-protected request, `lichen_coap_oscore_respond(&auth, ...)` is called. But `auth` was populated by `authorize_mutating` on the original request and is valid. However, at coap_dtn.c:119-123, when a non-OSCORE, non-local-admin request hits deaddrop_post, it sends an UNPROTECTED 4.01 via `lichen_coap_respond` even though the OSCORE option path already returned early via `authorize_mutating` for OSCORE requests that lack a context. This is correct — those paths are mutually exclusive. BUT: if `authorize_mutating` fails (returns < 0), it has already sent a response (4.01 via coap_oscore_send_unauthorized), and the caller returns immediately. No double-send. Verified correct.

After full review: no actual bugs found. This is a clean refactoring that correctly centralizes the OSCORE auth pattern.
